question.worked_solution:
First, recall that

$$
{lim}_{s\to 1}f(s)=[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 1}\sqrt{5-s} \\ {lim}_{s\to 1}\frac{{e}^{1-s}}{s} \\ {lim}_{s\to 1}\,(1+5s)^{1/(2s)}.\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we find the limits one by one.

- For the first component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 1}\sqrt{5-s} & =\sqrt{5-1} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 1}\frac{{e}^{1-s}}{s}=\frac{{e}^{1-1}}{1}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the third component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 1}\,(1+5s)^{1-s} & =(1+5\cdot 1)^{1-1} \\  & ={6}^{0} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{s\to 1}f(s)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
